findings.claim: The duration count is parsed outside the try, with a Unicode \d. A count of more than 4300 digits (for example '9'*5000 + 'd') makes int() raise ValueError, and kmctl new prints a traceback instead of a refusal. A non-ASCII digit such as '٣d' is accepted as 3 days.

The commands for rows r4 and r5 select fewer tests than they claim. In r4, -k freshness_valid deselects every test in tests/test_okf_fields.py. In r5, the second -k replaces the first, so test_init_block_names_freshness never runs. Each command runs one test. The r6 full suite does run the missing tests, so the behaviour is still gated, but the per-row stamps for r4 and r5 would stay green if the I4 test or the block broke.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
`--stale-after` and `--source` write the right fields in the shape the strict validator accepts.
Every refusal happens before anything is written.
`review_due._resolve` behaves exactly as before.
There are two non-blocking findings: a crash on an absurdly long duration (plus non-ASCII digits being accepted), and the commands for eval rows r4 and r5 not running the tests they name.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass; rows r1 to r6 pass; "stamp green: ece49c8e2de27fdca9301262e175b53502eaab1f9cf54cd6dfad1923e07f878f".
Read the whole diff of src, tests and docs against main.
Date edges, probed by calling `stale_after_time` directly: `1m` from Jan 31 gives Feb 28, or Feb 29 in 2028.
`11m` from Dec 31 gives Nov 30.
`2027-02-29` is refused; `2028-02-29` is accepted.
An offset timestamp is converted to UTC, and one without an offset is read as UTC.
A `now` with an offset still gives UTC output.
`9999-12-31T23:59:59-01:00` is refused (no UTC value).
`30D`, `' 30d'`, `20270115` and `2027-W03` are refused, and the message names the value.
A bare date counts as its midnight UTC, so today's date is refused; tomorrow's date is accepted.
Only the 5000-digit count crashes (f1).
Order of checks: `--key`, `--source` on a handoff, and `--stale-after` are all checked before the key lookup.
`_check_sources` runs before the section is created, the folder is made, or the file and log are written.
The refusal tests compare every .okf/*.md file, including log.md, before and after.
review_due: I copied the old `_resolve` into a script and compared it with the new one on 78 cases against this repo's tracked files.
The cases covered `/`, `..`, `.`, empty, a trailing slash, escaping the root, concept ids, `.md` added and folders.
Old and new agree on every case.
`kmctl review due --path /home/vscode/kmctl --json` gives byte-identical output with main's code and the worktree's code (13 due, all for "unverified").
Sources shape: `- resource: "PATH"` passes `okf_validate --strict` with no warning in test_new_freshness_valid, and the fields are a subset of ALLOWED_FIELDS.
JSON-quoted strings are valid YAML double-quoted scalars.
Eval rows: r1, r2 and r3 each run tests that assert their fails_when, and r3 includes the git commit test that checks the "source changed" reason.
For r4 and r5, see f2.
Help and docs: the `kmctl new practice --help` text is plain and complete.
The reference, tutorial, overview table and the ADR 0011 correction match the code.
ADR 0008's "14 days out" still holds as the default.
f1: The fix is to use `[0-9]+` (or re.ASCII) and to cap the count's length or move `int()` inside the try, so a long count is refused as too far in the future.
This is a plain fix, so it is non-blocking.
f2: The fix belongs to the eval rows, not the code.
The r4 command could be `uv run pytest "tests/test_new_concept.py::test_new_freshness_valid" tests/test_okf_fields.py -q`.
The r5 command needs node ids or a single `-k "block_names_freshness or freshness_documented"`.
This is non-blocking because r6 covers both tests.
`_check_sources` accepts any path on disk, including gitignored files and empty folders.
`review due` will then only report "source not resolved" for those.
The plan accepts this for untracked files, so I did not raise it as a finding.
